$comment: Combinatorial prompt parts. Composed as '{character} {situation}, {setting}.' Characters must be capitalized noun phrases; situations third-person-singular verb phrases; settings prepositional phrases. Keep that grammar and any combination reads correctly. charactersByGenre/settingsByGenre override the universal pools for genres where the contemporary-realist defaults would not make sense.

turns out to be the last person certified to operate a machine nobody will admit is still running
finds their own name in a record that predates them
must decide what a settlement is allowed to remember about how it began
is contacted by something patient enough to wait a lifetime for an answer
begins hearing their own voice from the next room
notices that a routine they have kept for years has been subtly altered
is welcomed by name somewhere they have never been
finds evidence of someone living very carefully inside their house

is warned by a stranger about one specific date
is given a key with no explanation and no matching lock
recognizes their own handwriting on something they never wrote

discovers a room in a building they have worked in for a decade

constraints: Write it without using the word "remember".
Do not name the central emotion anywhere in the piece.
Begin at the end and move backwards.
Let the narrator be wrong about something the reader can see.
Begin every paragraph with a concrete object.
Write it as a single unbroken sentence.
Include a list of at least six things.
Set the entire piece in one room.
Write it as a document: a form, a report, a set of instructions.
End on an image, not a line of dialogue.
The weather must change exactly once.
